### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **38** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `52534e463aed17833d1b2277c2976080ebe79f16` — the merge of head `da074fddd29cb2deb93744f0b69ad4f4cedb198c` into base `cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 52534e463aed17833d1b2277c2976080ebe79f16 && git checkout 52534e463aed17833d1b2277c2976080ebe79f16
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73 da074fddd29cb2deb93744f0b69ad4f4cedb198c && git checkout -B drift-repro cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73 && git merge --no-ff da074fddd29cb2deb93744f0b69ad4f4cedb198c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 这是预读，不是结论：Studio 编辑器那一部分还没进这个分支，终审等它进来后再做。
- 已读部分符合 #35896 / #35897 / #35899：声明了 `relatedLists` 就只显示列出的页签、按列的顺序；三个内置页签用对象名；一项可以带自己的标题和列；没声明的对象完全照旧。
- 有一处要先定：#35921 合并后，「被字段分组放进概览的主从子表在页签栏也保留一项」，碰上「声明了 relatedLists 就只显示列出的」，没列它时页签要不要出现，两张卡说法不一致。座位会决定是否需要问你。
- 要你做什么：现在不需要。

## 席位核对 — preliminary read (L1-c), no verdict · repo:objectstack#1 · head `da074fddd2` · 2026-11-20T19:10Z

The seat asked for this read before the Studio `RelatedListsEditor` part lands. The verdict is given on the head that carries that part, and only the delta from `da074fdd` is read then. The face: published schema (`object.zod.ts` `RelatedListEntrySchema`, new `related-list-entry.ts`, one `semantic/18` entry), Tier H (`docs/adr/0035`, `docs/adr/0085`), and `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The contract L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is the seat's.

### Owed before the final pass

1. **`Skills-docs:` line missing.** `Metadata-protocol: semantic` owes the body a third line (l1-face `skills-docs` FLAG). #35902 holds the skills and docs text for this epic, so the line is `Skills-docs: follow-up #35902`.
2. **A fork between this PR and #35921 (PR #35921, #35889 item 4), for the seat.** After #35921 a plain `master_detail` table that a field group places is a body table AND keeps its tab (「是不是还是应该不从选项卡中隐藏，始终显示」). Here, `deriveRelatedLists` keeps every unlisted body table (`if (list.isPrimary) all.push(list)`), and `arrangeDeclaredTabs` ranks an unlisted `related:` tab at `unlisted`. Once both are on `main`, an object that declares `relatedLists` without naming that child still shows its tab, after the listed ones. #35897 says a declared list shows only what it lists (「声明了 … 只显示列出来的」) and leaves only the field-area table alone (「不动字段区里由分组放进去的子表」). It says nothing about that table's tab. Neither card settles which rule wins. My reading: the tab follows `relatedLists` (unlisted ⇒ no tab), and the body table stays at its group. Whichever the seat picks, pin it with a test on the head that merges #35921.
3. **The editor part.** It must keep object entries and built-in names on save. Per the body, today the editor drops them, so this PR cannot land before that part is in (#35897 item 8, #35899 item 5).

### Nit

4. The PR body has no signature line (`repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · <session>`) above `Fixes #35897`.

### Read and fine so far

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`. `Fixes #35897` and `Fixes #35899` are one line each, which is the fold shape (both cards carry a claim naming the branch).
- **Spec.** An entry is a bare name or a strict `{ list, label?, columns? }` with aliases and guidance for `filter` / `sort`. A built-in name in the object form is refused by a regex lookahead, so the JSON schema keeps it (#35897 item 5). `columns` is non-empty, of non-empty strings.
- **Record page.** Undeclared or empty `relatedLists` leaves `deriveRelatedLists` and `arrangeDeclaredTabs` as identity, which is #35897 item 1 and the epic's 「没写新写法就照旧」. Attachments show only when listed and still need `enable.files`. Unlisted approvals and the stream keep their place at the end (the coordinator's line on #35897). `relatedList: false` on the FK still hides a list (item 7). The built-ins only reorder the existing attachment, approval and stream tabs, never a data table (item 4).
- **Columns and title.** An entry's `label` / `columns` override the FK's keys on the derived list, which feeds both the tab and a group-placed body table (#35899 items 2 and 3). Lint `related-list-column-unknown` refuses a column that is no field of the child (item 4).
- **Overlaps.** No `RecordDetailView.tsx` source hunk (only the harness test). `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` touches the `ObjectDefLike` type, the `synthTabs` return and the new `arrangeDeclaredTabs`, not the header (#35891) or `sides` (#35921). In `deriveRelatedLists.ts` the hunks are the order/visibility block, which #35921 also edits nearby (`isPrimary` / `isPlaceable` at the derive loop). Merge main after #35921 and re-run that file's tests.
- **Prose** (the changeset, the ADR-0035 and ADR-0085 notes, the migration entry) is read sentence by sentence against the diff at this head. The generated `content/docs/references/**` is checked by `check:generated`, not read by eye. Each matches. The approvals / stream "move-only" sentences rest on the coordinator's line on #35897, which the maintainer has not contradicted.
- **Gates.** At `da074fdd`: 13 success, 9 expected skip, 0 failed, 25 pending. Vitest was NOT MEASURED by L1.
